A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CTCL framework, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched, including the full generative-results table moved from v1 Appendix D to v2 Appendix K.

before.justification: v1 reports original downstream generation and classification experiments across five datasets, together with component ablations, scalability analyses, and synthetic examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds topic-assignment counts and qualitative controlled-generation examples in its appendices.

M1.justification: The conditional generator, topic model, DP finetuning, and histogram-guided generation remain unchanged. Appendix H restates the pipeline as pseudocode. Appendix F newly documents an unclassified bin used in the experiments, without establishing that this component was newly introduced.

E1.justification: The public training corpora and five downstream datasets remain unchanged. Appendix I adds a limited qualitative test scenario: generation before private finetuning under News, Chat, and Blog Post conditions with shared surfing-related keywords.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds Downstream DPFT to the privacy-budget comparison previously displaying only AUG-PE and CTCL in Figure 3, using already reported results. Comparator membership in the main benchmark tables is unchanged. Newly cited concurrent PE methods are explicitly not evaluated.

E3.justification: Original splits, metrics, training budgets, and model configurations remain unchanged. Additional analyses examine histogram noise of 10 versus 20 at PubMed ε = 4 and generation before finetuning with fixed keywords and varied document types. These introduce supplementary analysis settings, without establishing benchmark reruns.

E4.justification: Appendices D, F, and I add targeted checks of privacy-allocation sensitivity, topic coverage and unclassified documents, and document-type controllability. Appendix J extends the existing qualitative sample comparison. The original component ablations, MAUVE analysis, and scalability experiments remain intact.

E5.justification: There is no change to seed information, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing. Results remain point estimates; the additional privacy-noise discussion does not constitute statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged, including v1 Table 8 and v2 Table 14. Added findings include 86 unclassified Chatbot Arena documents, four Yelp documents, zero in the other datasets, and new generated examples. Appendix K incorrectly places DPFT below AUG-PE at ε = 4 despite Table 3 reporting 30.7 versus 30.3.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same DP definition and post-processing explanation. The added privacy-budget accounting examples introduce numerical elaboration, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central conclusion retain the same contributions: privacy-preserving synthesis using a lightweight conditional generator and topic model, avoiding billion-scale DP finetuning and domain-specific prompt engineering, with advantages across five domains and strong privacy settings.

C2.justification: The conclusion newly acknowledges weaker fluency and coherence than large prompted LLMs and discusses multimodal extensions. Appendices D, F, G, and I expand explanations of privacy allocation, topic coverage, pretraining costs, and the privacy rationale for different pretraining and finetuning conditions.

D1.justification: v2 adds code-access information, an explicit privacy-accountant implementation link, per-component privacy-budget details, and documentation of unclassified-topic handling. Appendix H supplies pseudocode for the existing procedure. Previously reported training hyperparameters, hardware, and training time remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work expands to concurrent PE improvements, private inference, synthetic-data filtering, and conditional generation, including Hou, Zou, Amin, Gao, and DeSalvo works from 2025. These additions refine the existing positioning; publication-metadata updates such as RedCoast do not represent new cited research.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives light language edits, updated cross-references, and a limitations/future-work extension. Appendices gain focused explanatory sections, and full generative results move from Appendix D to K. The main section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The appendix presentation is substantially expanded with privacy-allocation and topic-coverage tables, condition/output examples, extended synthetic-sample comparisons, three algorithm displays, and Figure 5. Existing full results are relocated and renumbered from Table 8 to Table 14, while the original main figures and tables remain largely intact.

improvement.justification: v2 improves auditability through code-access information, clearer privacy accounting, topic-coverage checks, and explicit fluency limitations. The gains are limited because the central method and benchmark evidence are unchanged. They outweigh localized defects: Appendix D leaves a δ value unfinished, and Appendix K incorrectly claims DPFT trails AUG-PE at ε = 4, contradicting the retained 30.7 versus 30.3 results.
